summary: Explains the default filter for undefined variables, that since 2.8 nested attribute access on undefined values stays undefined so default works on nested paths, and default(value, true) to also replace false or empty values.
questions: How do I give a variable a default value in a template?
How do I use a default for a nested key that might not exist?
How do I use a default when a variable is an empty string?
Why use role defaults instead of the default filter?

answer_card.title: Providing default values
answer_card.answer_md:
```jinja
{{ some_variable | default(5) }}
```

Since 2.8, accessing an attribute of an undefined value returns undefined, so nested defaults work: `{{ foo.bar.baz | default('DEFAULT') }}`.

To also replace false or empty-string values, pass `true`:

```jinja
{{ lookup('env', 'MY_USER') | default('admin', true) }}
```

In roles you can also use role defaults.
